sentences.text:
The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 15.05.2023 at about 1.30 p.m. Abu Bakar Gowhar @ Gowhar had been riding his Honda Dio bearing Reg.No.KA03JP4463 near Kalyan Nagar Flyover, Outer Ring Road, Bengaluru, a BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F4693 came at high speed and dashed behind his motor cycle, due to the impact, Abu Bakar Gowhar @
Gowhar fell down and wheel of the said SCCH5 bus ran over on his leg, as a result he succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
3. At the time of accident, deceased/Abu Bakar Gowhar @ Gowhar was aged about 26 years, hale and healthy, working at Swiggy and Dunzo, thereby earning Rs.50,000/ p.m.
petitioner is the mother of the deceased, due to untimely death of the deceased, she is put to great financial loss and mental agony.
Out of this accident crime No.82/2023 is registered against the driver of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F 4693lorry before the Banasawadi Traffic Police.
Respondent is the internal insurer is liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. SCCH5 4.

On service of notice, respondent being the internal insurer of the BMTC has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioner and also denied occurrence of the accident,
rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F4693.
Further stated that, deceased was wholly and solely responsible for the accident.

Further denied age,
occupation and income of the deceased, claim made by the petitioner is higher side, hence his petition is not maintainable, further denies relationship of petitioner with the deceased.
Further stated that, on humanitarian grounds, respondent corporation has paid exgratia amount of Rs.25,000/ to the petitioner.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH5 5.

On going through the rival pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.Whether Petitioner proves that, deceased Abu Bakar Gowhar @ Gowhar, S/o.
Abubakar Siddiq Lalu Bai Gari died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.05.2023 at about 1.30 p.m.

When deceased was proceeding on his motor cycle near Kalyan Nagar Flyover, Outer Ring Road, Bengaluru City, at that time, one BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F4693 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:
In order to prove her case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW1, in her SCCH5 chiefexamination she has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of medical intimation to the police is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of P.M. is marked as Ex.P.10,
copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.11.
9.
In crossexamination she admits that, she has not seen the accident, she cannot say that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of her son, but denied that, it is a false case.
Further admits that, first informant has not seen the accident.

The police papers marked at SCCH5 Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 speaks that very accident is occurred due to negligency of the bus driver, charge sheet is against him, holding that, due to negligency of the bus driver, this accident is occurred.
10. On the other hand, driver of the respondent corporation has appeared before this court and deposed his evidence as per RW1 wherein he has not denied the place, date and time of the accident.
Even there is no denial of place, date and time of the accident in written statement.
Further deposed that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the deceased Abu Bakar Gowhar.

11. In crossexamination deposed that, he had been to Banasawadi police station to lodge the complaint, but they have not received the same, then he lodged the SCCH5 complaint before the Commissioner of Police having copy of such complaint with him, but not produced before the court.
Further admits that, FIR and charge sheet are against him, department enquiry is pending against him.
Further denied that, in order to escape from the liability deposing false evidence.

Further it is Hurbanu Lalu Bai Gari A.B vs B.M.T.C on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3770316/
3 noticed that, while moving on a highway, bus is dashed against hind side of the motor cycle caused this accident which runs about 53 feet even after crossing the accident spot.

sentences.text: 12. During argument counsel for respondent submitted that, there is contributory negligence of the deceased, to some extent responsibility shall be shifted against him, but to shift the liability against the deceased, to some extent there is no substantive evidence on record.
In crossexamination PW 1 has shown her SCCH5 innocence about the nature of the accident.
Only on the basis of such innocence and also for not examining of the any of the eyewitness it cannot be hold that, there is negligency of the deceased.
Under such circumstances, this court comes to the conclusion that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the BMTC Bus driver.
Hence I have answered the above issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
As per the case of the petitioner, deceased Abu Bakar Gowhar @ Gowhar was aged about 26 years at the time of accident.

In this regard she has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12 wherein year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 1996, the alleged accident is occurred on 15.05.2023, hence relying on Ex.P.12 age of the deceased is SCCH5 considered as 27 years at the time of his death and multiplier 17 is applicable with reference to case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Further there is say of the petitioner stating that, her son had monthly income of Rs.50,000/ by way of working in Swiggy and Dunzo, but to prove the said facts not produced any documents.
Hence considering the same, this court relied upon the Karnataka Minimum Wages for the year 202324.

In the case on hand, petitioner is coolie, nature of work is not mentioned in the petition,
so that, he comes under the category semi skilled worker category.

Very accident is occurred on 15.05.2023, accordingly as on the date of accident including dearness allowances for unskilled workers SCCH5 minimum wages for a month will come to Rs.15,583/, so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency 15.
Petitioner is a mother of the deceased, to prove the said fact, she has furnished copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, hence she will become dependent on the income of the deceased.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased is bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

16. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear SCCH5 that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

17. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.

sentences.text:
(i) Monthly Income Rs.15,583/
(ii) 40% of (i) above if Rs.15,583/ (+) added to the Rs.6,233/ = monthly income as Rs.21,816/
future prospects (iii) 1/2 of (ii) of the Rs.21,816/ () same to be deducted Rs.10,908/ = towards personal and living expenses SCCH5
Monthly income Rs.10,908/ p.m (iv) Compensation after Rs.10,908/ x Rs.22,25,232/ multiplier of 17 is 12 x 17 applied 18.

Hence, petitioner being the mother of the deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/ towards for loss of filial consortium, further she is entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/ and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/.
19. In crossexamination PW1 admits that, after the accident she has received the compensation amount of Rs.25,000/.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that, it is just and necessary to deduct the same in the award amount.
SCCH5 20.

The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 22,25,23200 2.
Loss of filial consortium 40,00000 3. Loss of Estate 15,00000 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,00000 Total 22,95,23200 LessCompensation 25,00000 paid by BMTC Grand Total 22,70,23200 21.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,70,232/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount,
22.

In the case on hand, respondent being the internal insurer of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA 01 SCCH5 F4693 is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3: Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above issues No.1 and 2

, I proceed to pass the following:
